talks.title: 🇬🇧 Dissecting and Comparing different Binaries to Malware Analysis Filipi Pires
talks.teaser: Presents 🇬🇧 Dissecting and Comparing different Binaries to Malware Analysis Filipi Pires and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Analysis Foundations

Filipi Pires argues malware analysts must understand core concepts behind debuggers and disassemblers. He defines threats per ISO standards and stresses that samples—code, applications, or binaries—are the starting artifact whose maliciousness must be determined.

Static Versus Dynamic Analysis

After identifying malware versus benign files or maldocs, analysts choose static statistical analysis or dynamic execution analysis. Reverse engineering techniques support both approaches.

Documentation for Defense

Pires recommends recording every analysis step to capture attacker techniques, support reporting to management, enable conference talks, and improve defenses by revealing which security controls were bypassed.

Threat Intelligence Value

Structured findings feed cyber threat intelligence and resilience programs. Static binary review helps threat hunters understand how attackers use binaries to explore environments and which libraries or functions appear in malicious samples.

talks.title: 🇬🇧 What’s Next after Domain Admin?
talks.teaser: Reviews 🇬🇧 Whats Next after Domain Admin and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
From Domain Admin to Azure

Venkat Raman Kumar (Red Wolf) and Tiramin describe pentest patterns where MSOL accounts with directory replication privileges led not to on-prem domain admin goals but straight into Azure AD. They argue clients now expect cloud compromise beyond traditional AD takeover because tenants hold PII, financial data, and multi-domain scope.

Hybrid Identity Foundations

The talk covers Azure AD versus on-premises AD differences—tenants instead of forests, SAML/OIDC instead of Kerberos, and REST APIs instead of LDAP. Hybrid sync uses password hash sync, pass-through authentication, or AD FS federation to unify identities across environments.

Reconnaissance Techniques

Unauthenticated checks include login-page redirects and tenant ID lookups via open endpoints. AADInternals enumerates authentication types, domains per tenant, and Azure subdomains via tools like MicroBurst. After DA access, NTDS dumps yield credentials testable against Azure; BloodHound and AzureHound map hybrid attack paths and Global Administrator holders.

Exploiting Azure AD Connect

Azure AD Connect creates paired service accounts whose passwords live in LSA secrets or local databases. Compromising these sync accounts bridges on-prem DA to cloud administration, including creating synced users in domains not yet owned on-premises.

talks.title: 🇬🇧 JUST Hackers things with Jayson E Street
talks.teaser: Investigates 🇬🇧 JUST Hackers things with Jayson E Street and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Session format

Jayson E Street fills a last-minute lehack slot with an unfiltered Q&A, offering swag and randomly selecting audience questioners if needed. He says he is not a famous hacker but shares hard-won lessons, citing the proverb that wise people learn from others' mistakes.

Costly early mistake

Asked about expensive professional failures, he recounts running nmap during an early vulnerability assessment that crashed a client Cisco router, ending the engagement. The story underscores careful scoping before network scanning.

Underrated hacker value

On the most underrated hacker trait, he answers sharing. Curiosity defines hackers, but too many talk themselves out of contributing because topics seem covered or audiences uninterested. He urges diverse voices to publish talks and tribal knowledge so the community accumulates more data than a narrow speaker circuit provides.

Physical testing mindset

He confirms bank laptop-theft social engineering work and describes pre-engagement imposter syndrome and client-focused intent rather than personal glory before red-team physical entries.
